name: Philip
overview: Philip was a male figure in the early Christian church, uniquely chosen to serve the widows of the Hellenistic Jews, demonstrating his role in addressing practical needs within the community. He is also recognized as "the evangelist," highlighting his significant role in spreading the gospel. His tribal affiliation is not recorded in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: Philip is the only name recorded for this individual, with no specific meaning provided in the biblical text. Therefore, his name is simply acknowledged as a proper name without additional significance noted.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Philip beyond what is listed in his unique role of serving widows. No other personal relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Philip's selection to serve the widows of the Hellenistic Jews underscores his trusted position in the early church to care for vulnerable members. Being called "the evangelist" further emphasizes his important ministry in proclaiming the gospel message to others. Together, these roles highlight his multifaceted contribution to the growth and nurturing of the early Christian community.
